chapter: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
title: Cab slaps Dizzy, Dizzy draws a knife and leaves the band
summary: Milt tells how Cab slapped Dizzy, who pulled a knife that Milt deflected; Cab found a trickle of blood and made a fuss, and Dizzy left.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: He had all them people there from the stage, doing that Cab Calloway Caravan...
Musical. And then the people from WOR, some of the executives were there -- they were thinking about renewing the show.
And all that in front of ...(?)...
Anyway, he hit... Cab slapped Dizzy, and that's when the altercation started about the knife, and he

really would have killed him if the guys hadn't got to him. Because I couldn't hold Dizzy. I tried to stop him, and the only thing I'd say is... I was standing right by when Dizzy went to hit him with the knife, and all I did, my hand just deflected the knife so it didn't go in Cab's stomach...

And when he goes in the dressing room, the valet is taking off his... He wore heavy underwear for perspiration. And when he looked at it, he saw this little trickle of blood. And he looked at that, he looked at the cut on those drawers, and he could see about where the spot was. He didn't know because he was all warm and hot...
Cab. So when he looked at the spot where it was, he laid down. And he said, 'Can you see that? Right there -- it's a little bit of...a trickle, whatever.

Just a little spot, but nothing much. That's when Cab went, 'Oh, Lawdy! He cut me. Keep me from dying. Get the doctor. Get the police. Get that Governor. Get the Sheriff. Call the Army. Get the Navy!'

So they said, "Well, get him out of the theatre." So they went to talk to him. They said, "Where he's at?" "Resting." Mister Wright said, "You know he can't rest in there." Then he said ...(?)..., "Resting? He could have killed Cab." And he was furious. And they went around, the Cotton Club boys -- they all was against Dizzy. "That's a shame. Look, man, we're all just trying to make a living. Send him up to Sing-Sing..." Dizzy's family was there.

Yeah, and his sister was up... It was sad. His sister lived up in there somewhere. There was his sister and his wife, and they had... They said, "Well, get your things." Well, Dizzy was in the dressing room with us, or the next room, and he got his belongings and everything. And they said, "Well, patch it up." He said, "Well, they could have patched it up if he just wouldn't have cut him." Because you can't have a killer on the stage. [LAUGHS]
